brief: Find struggling Indian startups TVF can salvage, prioritising media, creators, consumer businesses, software and AI products and physical proximity to the Andheri West office. Upfront purchase price must be strictly below INR 1 crore. Unknown price requires review; funding, revenue and headcount never establish purchase price. Apollo spending is paused.

geography.home_region: India, prioritising Andheri West and Mumbai
geography.guidance: Mumbai proximity ranks candidates; another Indian city is not excluded. A confirmed foreign headquarters is excluded. Unconfirmed location remains a research gap.

rubric.label: Evidence of current distress
rubric.guidance: Public distress evidence weighted by recency: up to 6 months full, 6-12 months 75%, 12-24 months 25%. Funding silence or a failed website alone is not confirmed distress.

rubric.label: TVF fit: media, creators, consumer, software and AI
rubric.guidance: Sector words from the company and its coverage. Fit is a research priority, not proof that TVF can revive the business.

rubric.label: A product, users, team or assets worth preserving
rubric.guidance: Dated, sourced asset evidence from a reviewer, or an app with recent updates and at least 1,000 ratings. A working homepage alone earns no salvage points.

rubric.label: Documented upfront price below INR 1 crore
rubric.guidance: Full points only for a dated asking price or founder quote with its source, checked within 90 days. Exactly INR 1 crore fails. Funding and revenue are not acquisition prices. Unknown price scores zero and stays unconfirmed.

rubric.label: Proximity to TVF's Andheri West office
rubric.guidance: Andheri West/Oshiwara/Lokhandwala/Versova 100%; adjacent western suburbs 80%; other Mumbai 60%; Thane/Navi Mumbai 40%; other India 10%; unknown 0. Address evidence required for neighbourhood points. These are bands, not measured distances.

rubric.label: Verified founder or decision-maker contact
rubric.guidance: Apollo-verified current founder/decision-maker contact; existing contact policy remains in force.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: raised an ordinary round in the last twelve months
score_modifiers.guidance: A company that closed a normal round in the last year is not out of runway, whatever else a headline says. Bridge and down rounds do not count here; they are distress.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: shut down more than a year ago
score_modifiers.guidance: A company that closed a year or more ago has usually lost its team and its users. Its brand or code may still be worth a conversation, so this lowers the score rather than ruling it out.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: no public sign of struggle
score_modifiers.guidance: Its coverage and its website were read and nothing shows struggle: no shutdown, layoffs, salary delays, down or rescue round, sale talks, pivot, and it has not gone quiet. The brief is startups that are struggling, so a healthy Mumbai startup is ranked below the review line instead of riding its fit and a small round into it. Added 2026-09-17 after the first list: 57 of 59 Mumbai-confirmed leads showed no sign of struggle. Weekly harvests keep reading its news; the day a headline shows trouble, the penalty lifts.

gates.label: Not a unicorn, a listed company or a big group's unit
gates.guidance: A round of $50M or more in its headlines, 'unicorn' or a listing in them, or a name in startup_discovery.major_companies. Those are not acquisitions for little to no resources.

gates.label: Not already sold
gates.guidance: A headline that another company acquired it. The sale is history, not an opportunity.

gates.label: Not long gone
gates.guidance: Fires when the newest sign of life -- a headline, a working website -- is more than three years old.

gates.label: Upfront purchase price strictly below INR 1 crore

startup_discovery.guidance: Historical news-discovery configuration. New companies come only from Apollo; sector tiers, publishers and event windows remain inputs to named-company qualification.

startup ("shuts down" OR "shut down" OR "shuts shop" OR "winds down" OR "ceases operations" OR "halts operations")
startup ("salary delays" OR "delayed salaries" OR "unpaid salaries" OR "salaries unpaid" OR "delays salaries")

startup India ("down round" OR "valuation cut" OR "rescue funding" OR "distress sale" OR "fire sale" OR "bridge round")
startup India ("acqui-hire" OR acquihire OR "in talks to be acquired" OR "explores sale")
Mumbai startup (layoffs OR "lays off" OR "shuts down" OR "shut down" OR insolvency OR "salary delays" OR "winds down")

funding_queries.query: "Mumbai-based" startup raises (seed OR "pre-seed" OR angel OR "pre-Series A")
"Mumbai-based" (D2C OR brand OR app OR platform) raises (seed OR angel OR "pre-Series A" OR "Series A")
"Mumbai-based" (media OR content OR gaming OR edtech OR creator OR entertainment OR audio) startup raises

1.label: Media, creator, consumer, software or AI business

0.label: Businesses TVF's audience does not move

sources.name: Apollo.io company and decision-maker search
sources.detail: tools/discover_apollo.py uses this project's saved constraints; contact roles and verified work addresses come from Apollo.

self_exclusion.guidance: Same affiliates as Segment 1 must never enter this pool either. In this segment 'tvf' is also a whole-word pattern: startup news calls TVF 'TVF', and the first dry run (2026-09-17) put it on its own acquisition list. Whole-word matching keeps names like TVFoods out of reach.

enrichment.guidance: Spending paused by owner, 16 November 2026. Enable only after an explicit new budget. Both manual and automatic reveals require current distress, salvage evidence and Indian headquarters. Unknown acquisition price stays a research gap. Owner, 16 November 2026: do not use any Apollo credits. All paid sourcing is paused until a new explicit budget is authorised. Owner, 16 November 2026: capped pilot authorised, maximum 100 credits total split 50 Clipping and 50 Startup; preserve at least 700 balance. Remain disabled until current balance is verified; this is not recurring spending authorisation.

sender.name: SET_ME
sender.title: Corporate Development, The Viral Fever
sender.postal_address: SET_ME street address for the email footer (CAN-SPAM)
sender.guidance: Sender name and title for the shared sign-off. The address is retained as an optional footer field and omitted from the default email footer (owner, 2026-10-09). The sending address comes from the connected Gmail account.

send_window.guidance: Owner, 2026-10-12: "I want you to send mails to the sender's time region between 10 to 10:30AM and that must be randmized not like all mail going at 10:15 some must be going at 10:17 some at 10:13 and so on after approval implement it". Each approved email goes out at its own random second between start and end on its RECIPIENT's clock (10:00 in Mumbai is 05:30 in London, too early to be read), drawn when it is approved and shown in Approved as "Goes out", with the time in India beside it. Where the recipient is comes from what the lead holds -- the person's own Apollo record, the company's state or city, a phone's area code, its country -- and the reason is kept on the email (tools/send_window.py). Monday to Friday on the recipient's clock (weekdays_only): an approval after today's window, or at a weekend, takes the next weekday's. An email whose window passes unsent (the server down, its address at its daily limit) moves to the next window at a new random time, never later the same day. Never two emails from one address closer than min_gap_seconds; never one sooner than min_lead_seconds after its approval. To send on the sender's clock instead (every email 10:00-10:30 India time) set timezone_of to "sender"; to switch the window off set enabled to false -- the stored times are cleared and approvals go out as soon as they can, as before. docs/runbook.md, "Goes out". Sending is paused for this project (sending_paused). Its startups are in Mumbai and elsewhere in India, so one that names no country is taken to be Indian (assumed_country). Owner, 2026-11-13: follow-ups go only on Saturday (recipient's clock), up to 50 per sending address; first emails go Monday to Friday (followup_day, followup_daily_cap). Owner, 2026-11-16: allow two emails per minute per connected account: a minimum 30-second gap, with zero extra scheduling padding. Existing sending windows and daily limits remain.

outreach.subject_max_words_guidance: The owner, 2026-10-13: "subject for all emails for all services should be less than 5 or equal to 5 words". Every rendered subject is checked against this (tools/draft_render.capped_subject): one over it uses its template's subject_fallback, and one still over it is not drafted, so a longer subject never ships. "Re:" in front of a follow-up is not counted. The owner, 2026-11-26: drafted subjects under 8 words (7 at most); a subject a person writes may be any length (approval no longer checks it).

templates.subject: A conversation worth having
templates.guidance: First touch. Deliberately ambiguous about acquisition - founders hear 'strategic' and choose how to read it. Human-approved per draft like every template. Subject (owner, 2026-10-13): "A conversation worth having", at most five words and no company name.

templates.subject: Re: {{opener_subject}}
templates.guidance: The follow-up to the corporate development note: the same voice and the same 20-minute ask.

follow_ups.guidance: Owner, 2026-10-23: "Make follo ups for all", after "set only 1 follow up after 4 days" for LCX Clipping. One follow-up, four days after the first email went out with no reply, in the same Gmail thread ("Re: <the first email's subject>"), from the same address, signed by the person whose Gmail the thread is in. It is a draft in the Follow-ups tab and needs approval like any email. Any reply stops it at once (an auto-reply lets it resume); Stop follow-ups ends the thread by hand; the database refuses one after a reply (sql/23).

outreach.guidance: Identical pipeline to Segment 1: drafted -> human-approved -> sent, one touch per company enforced by the database. The footer -- the sign-off -- is one setting for the whole segment (outreach.footer.text), edited in the app under Outreach -> Footer; templates end with {{footer}}.

footer.guidance: Owner decision 2026-10-09: the sign-off, with the postal address omitted. The owner, 2026-10-13: the opt-out line is removed from every project's footer ("remove the last line from every single service"); any reply that is not neutral still stops all mail to that address. Edited in Outreach -> Footer. Postal addresses are optional; templates end with {{footer}}.

outreach.default_cc_guidance: The owner, 2026-10-22: "add a feature to cc someone from the software itself. Make default cc to the email amritanshv@lightscameraexperiment.com and obvio make a toggle to switch that off". Every email of this project is copied to these addresses unless the person approving it switches that off in the email (the CC toggle) or changes the list. The list an email is approved with is the one it goes out with (outreach.cc, sql/39, frozen at approval): changing this default never changes an email already approved. A reply from one of these addresses is not taken for the recipient's reply. [] copies nobody by default.

sourcing.guidance: Owner decision 2026-10-19: all new leads and contacts come from Apollo. Existing project constraints, gates and scoring remain. Company websites and news verify already-known leads; they do not discover new ones. Clipping is exempt. Owner, 2026-10-23: a lead a person found on their own is the exception ("send custom mail to a lead that we find on our own, as in lead is not generated by software"): Leads -> Add a lead adds it by hand with source 'manual', and the address that person typed in (contacts source 'manual', verifier 'person') may be written to (sql/42, tools/manual_lead.py). Nothing automatic adds a manual lead.

apollo_discovery.guidance: Researched against Apollo's Organization Search documentation, 16 November 2026. Within each search rotation: Mumbai first, then Navi Mumbai/Thane, then India; teams 1-50. Each area has media/creator/consumer and software/AI searches, prioritising at least 10% headcount decline over 12 months, plus searches without that requirement for missing history. Decline is a screening hint, never proof of distress or acquisition price. No Indian postcode or radius filter: use sourced office addresses for Andheri proximity scoring. No revenue, funding or founding-year cutoff; no inference that these establish an asking price. Full company availability and price below INR 1 crore require dated evidence. Owner, 16 November 2026: do not use any Apollo credits. All paid sourcing is paused until a new explicit budget is authorised.

startup_acquisition.office_address: Contagious Online Media Network Pvt Ltd., 702, 7th Floor, A Wing, Fortune Terraces, Opp. Citi Mall, New Link Rd, Andheri West, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400053
startup_acquisition.deal_types: Full company acquisitions only. Exclude asset-only purchases, acqui-hires, minority equity and revenue share.
startup_acquisition.proximity_method: Address/neighbourhood bands, not measured kilometres or travel time. City-only evidence earns only city-level points.
